scenario: Clients that never read their responses, against release servers (review V1). (a) 512 clients, defaults (512 connections, 10 s write stall, 100 requests per connection), each pipelining 5,000 GET /health with SO_RCVBUF 1 KiB. (b) up to 512 clients pipelining 20 GET /jobs?limit=1000 (275 KB answers), defaults. (c) as (b) with 400 clients against --max-connections 256. /health sampled every ~1.5 s; server-side established connections counted with lsof.

machine.note: macOS caps the accept queue at 128 (kern.ipc.somaxconn), so connections beyond the cap plus 128 are reset by the kernel

reading: (a) /health answered at once throughout and the server closed all 512 (each connection ends after its 100th answer). (b) connections whose large answers stalled were closed ~10 s after their writes stopped (471 -> 0 by t+16 s). (c) with every slot held, /health was refused by the kernel's full accept queue until the first stalled batch closed; the first 200 came at t+15 s. Client-side 'closed' counts in (b) and (c) undercount: the client must drain the server's queued bytes before it sees EOF; the server-side counts are the measure.
